findings.summary: All four review control schemas are now byte-bound to the frozen commit. Post-frozen mutations of review_request.schema.json, review_registry.schema.json, review_artifact.schema.json or acceptance_decision.schema.json make canonical --require-ready fail before acceptance.

Review scope and pre-issued reviewer slots remain byte-bound through review_request.json. Removing CONTENT_GOVERNANCE.md from scope or replacing reviewer identities, then recomputing digest, registry and artifacts, fails canonical --require-ready.

Direct capability prohibitions reject the three declared authorization flags independently of schema wording, while byte-binding acceptance_decision.schema.json rejects a newly introduced runtime_storage_write_authorized field.

Temporal strictness is not evaluated over the actual union. With recomputed ledger/package locks, a child primary interval 1502-08-01 through 1502-08-15 plus an alternative 1502-08-15 through 1502-08-31 is accepted as a refinement of the predecessor interval 1502-08-01 through 1502-08-31. The possible-set union is unchanged, but predecessor_contained_by_child is false because no single child member contains the whole predecessor. Pairwise containment therefore mistakes a representation split for strict narrowing.

Prior independent-review history is mutable after the frozen revision. In a legitimate synthetic READY/ACCEPT descendant, deleting the round-1 through round-3 entries from review_registry.prior_reviews still makes canonical --require-ready succeed; deleting their artifact files also has no effect once their entries are removed. The validator requires only that the remaining prior artifacts collectively cover both tracks, so append-only audit history is not enforced against the frozen registry or an explicit closed prior-review set.

Finding counters are reconciled, current artifacts are schema- and SHA-bound, paths reject traversal and symlinks, reviewer instances and tracks are distinct, frozen commit/tree/digest identity is exact, and custom package/schema inputs cannot borrow canonical READY evidence.

Complete semantic locks, closed collection IDs, duplicate-key rejection, source artifact/locator integrity, globally unique IDs, bidirectional Claim/EvidenceLink/Uncertainty closure, non-local uncertainty rejection, append-only revision replay, deterministic frontier, NARROW/REJECT frozen binding and direct capability prohibitions remain fail-closed.

The remote PR and branch both point to the supplied commit; its tree and independently replayed reviewed-content digest are exact. The fixture validator passes, canonical --require-ready fails closed before reviews, 54 focused tests pass, Release Check passes, all 10 pull-request workflow runs succeeded, git diff --check passes, and frozen #329/#330, Gate C and project_state.json boundaries are unchanged.

conclusion: The exact frozen candidate closes the round-4 mutable-control-schema defect and preserves the earlier integrity controls, with green focused, release and GitHub checks. However, temporal union strictness still accepts a representation-only interval split as refinement, and prior independent-review audit history can be erased after the frozen revision while canonical READY remains valid. These two material fail-open paths prevent READY.
